audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant' initial (non-strict) is correct: Howson 2017 JIPA pp. 364-365 (now obtained, open access) states primary stress always on the first syllable with exceptions only in loanwords and a few native compounds, plus penult secondary stress in 4+ syllable words; Dolgopolov 2023 and the Wikipedia text (traced to Šewc-Schuster 1984:27-28) agree. The weakness is provenance, not substance: the deciding citation is Wikipedia, the record's quote/cite/loc/grade fields are empty, and one of the three stitched sentences (secondary stress) comes from an uncitated Wikipedia paragraph rather than Šewc-Schuster. Action: re-cite the record to Howson 2017:364-365 (verbatim quote above), keep kind unchanged, and upgrade the strength of the evidence; Šewc-Schuster 1984 / Schuster-Šewc 1996 remain print-only works still to obtain for a first-hand reference-grammar quote. no reclassification and no identity issue.
audit.second_reader_evidence: Independent re-check of all three downloaded files under (nothing was 'held' before our check; the weight-sensitive languages/the full catalog/our earlier reading have no uppe1395 dir)..): line 357 '===Stress===' has exactly two bullets, 'Words consisting of up to three syllables are stressed on the first syllable.{{sfnp|Šewc-Schuster|1984|p=27}}' and 'Foreign words, such as student /stuˈdɛnt/.. preserve their original accent.{{sfnp|Šewc-Schuster|1984|p=28}}'; the record's middle sentence 'In four-syllable or longer words, a secondary stress appears on the penultimate syllable' is verbatim at line 363 but in the separate '=== Prosody ==

sources.citation: Wikipedia, Upper Sorbian language, Stress section (citing Sewc-Schuster 1984:27-28), re-read 2026-08-31
sources.quote: Words consisting of up to three syllables are stressed on the first syllable. ... In four-syllable or longer words, a secondary stress appears on the penultimate syllable. ... Foreign words, such as student /stu'dent/ 'student', preserve their original accent.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Upper Sorbian language', raw wikitext downloaded 2026-09-16 (the record's deciding source).
sources.quote: Stress section: up-to-three-syllable words stressed on first syllable; foreign words keep original accent. Prosody section (uncited): stress expiratory, mainly first syllable; secondary stress on penult in 4+ syllable words; compounds secondary on first syllable of second element; superlative naj- takes main stress; prepositions attract stress from mono/disyllabic nouns; loanwords keep source stress (literaˈtura, šoˈfer).

sources.citation: Dolgopolov, Pavel I. 2023. Udarenie v verkhneluzhitskom iazyke v svete osobennostei verkhneluzhitskogo stikhoslozheniia [Stress in Upper Sorbian in the light of some features of Upper Sorbian versification]. In: Slavianskii mir: obshchnost' i mnogoobrazie (young-scholars conference, Institute of Slavic Studies RAS), 2023(2): 163-166. doi:10.31168/2619-0869.2023.2.05 (open PDF at inslav.ru).
sources.quote: Upper Sorbian 'is traditionally described as having, with rare exceptions [fn: Šewc-Schuster 1984], fixed stress on the first syllable' (fn 3: Stone 1993). Small Praat study (15 min of read prose/verse from YouTube): strong phrase-final lengthening of unstressed syllables explains rhyming of third syllables of trisyllables; author concludes it is wrong to posit a special secondary stress on the third syllable of trisyllables, and notes that acoustic correlates of Upper Sorbian stress have not been specifically studied.

sources.citation: Howson, Phil. 2017. Upper Sorbian (Illustrations of the IPA). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 47(3): 359-367. doi:10.1017/S0025100316000414 (Cambridge Core open access).
sources.quote: 'In general, primary stress always falls on the first syllable (e.g. wysoke [ˈwɨsokə] 'high neut'.) and its phonetic realization is a rising or higher pitch on the stressed syllable. There are a few exceptions to stress placement in Sorbian: stress can fall on a syllable besides the first in loan words (e.g. uniwersita [uniˈʋeɐsita] 'University'); there are also a small number of indigenous compounds which bear stress on a different syllable (e.g. bohužel [bohuˈʒel] 'unfortunately'), although stress often appears on the first syllable in these compounds as well ... Secondary stress is also ass

tone.quote: 2.1.2. В литературных верхнелужицком и нижнелужицком языках и в большинстве диалектов представлено фиксированное динамическое ударение на первом слоге слова или тактовой группы — например, сочетания существительных и местоимений с односложными и реже двусложными предлогами, ср.: в.-луж. 'město ‛город’, 'do města ‛в город’, 'na dźěle ‛на работе’. [...] В тактовых группах, содержащих не менее трех слогов, наряду с главным факультативно реализуется также слабое второстепенное ударение, которое, как правило, падает на предпоследний слог: 'domo'wina ‛родина’.
tone.translation: 2.1.2. Literary Upper Sorbian and Lower Sorbian and most dialects have fixed dynamic (expiratory) stress on the first syllable of the word or clitic group - e.g. combinations of nouns and pronouns with monosyllabic and, more rarely, disyllabic prepositions, cf. USo. 'město 'town', 'do města 'to town', 'na dźěle 'at work'. [...] In clitic groups of three or more syllables a weak secondary stress is optionally realised alongside the main one, as a rule on the penultimate syllable: 'domo'wina 'homeland'.
tone.n_tones: 0 (accent type stated as dynamic stress; no tones)

Ob otrazhenii drevnikh kolichestvennykh i intonatsionnykh otnoshenii v verkhneluzhitskom iazyke [On the reflection of the old quantity and intonation relations in Upper Sorbian]. In L. E. Kalnyn' (ed.), Serbo-luzhitskii lingvisticheskii sbornik, 54-83. Moskva: Izdatel'stvo AN SSSR.

tone.quote: То, что [ó] и [ě], появляющиеся вместо о и е в закрытых слогах, также [ó] и [ě] в рефлексах праславянских *tort, *tolt, *tert, *telt, отражают старые долготы, возникшие или в результате падения «еров», или как продолжение древнейших интонационных отношений, с достаточной убедительностью было показано в целом ряде работ. [...] Таким образом, строгое изучение рефлексов старых долгот в верхнелужицком языке возможно лишь путем последовательного снятия пластов с одновременным тщательным историческим и диалектологическим исследованием. Задача статьи — показать некоторые возможности и пути такого исследования.
tone.locator: p. 54, first paragraph, and p. 55 first full paragraph
tone.translation: That [ó] and [ě], which appear instead of o and e in closed syllables, and likewise [ó] and [ě] in the reflexes of Proto-Slavic *tort, *tolt, *tert, *telt, reflect old lengths that arose either from the fall of the jers or as the continuation of the oldest intonational (tonal) relations, has been shown convincingly enough in a whole series of works. [...] Thus a rigorous study of the reflexes of the old lengths in Upper Sorbian is possible only by successively removing the layers, together with careful historical and dialectological investigation. The aim of the article is to show some possibilities and paths of such an investigation.
